result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B has a clear brand anchor: a deep seaweed-green hero on a warm cream page, with readable cream type. That feels deliberate and avoids the usual health-food look, though using both lime and orange as accents dilutes it a little. A has good tinted neutrals and a dark-green Shop now button, but its three product cards use loud, unrelated colors (sage, lime, orange) that fight for attention, and the orange accent shows up in several places. B's cards aren't visible in its screenshot, so its item 6 score is a middle-of-the-range estimate. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A builds a strong identity around one deep seaweed-green, which avoids the leaf-green default, and it sets that against a tinted cream. Orange is held to the logo and the button, though the lime headline adds a second accent. A's product cards are not visible in the screenshot, so I scored that item low. B is warm, readable and tasteful, but its orange shows up in several places, and its three cards use loud unrelated fills (sage, lime, orange), which is exactly what the last rubric item penalizes.
